citation: J. Mountford, 'Mrs. O'Leary's residence, No. 137 DeKoven St., where the great fire originated', stereograph, Chicago, 1871. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-USZ62-57060 (cph 3b04891).
author: J. Mountford, photographer (the card's mount)
date: [October-November 1871] (after the fire: the block behind the cottages is burnt out)
describes_date: 1871, just after the fire of 8-9 October
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. The right half of the card is committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3689/loc_3b04891_oleary_cottage_right.jpg.
locator: The right half of the card: the two O'Leary cottages from the burnt lots north-east of them, the rear cottage's east side and north gable nearest, the front cottage beyond at left, fences, a crowd and the wash hung out in the yard, the houses across DeKoven Street at right.
rights_note: The Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.' A photograph published in 1871.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-20 (T-3689) from the Library's TIFF of the whole card (1536 x 796 px, tile.loc.gov service/pnp/cph/3b00000/3b04000/3b04891); the right half cropped and committed at 655 x 650 px, sha256 a26dd0f8882462ffb06f67297e5d19de6d8da8e8abd434711430cae68fea6d62.
note: The one photograph found of the cottages where the fire began, taken in the burnt block within weeks of the fire. Small and soft; monochrome.
what_it_supplies: the two cottages' arrangement, roofs, chimneys and weatherboarding
that they stood after the fire
what_it_does_not_supply: the cottages' street fronts and west sides
